mentl/ef842ff:
Face 7, pinned by the first coredump autopsy (4.0GB image at trap).
Pass-2 #8/#9 died in lower at assoc_row with an indirect call type
mismatch: heap_ptr read 0x2250 from the corpse — the bump pointer had
crossed 2^32 and was minting records over the init-built fn-record
region; assoc_row's own record held [1839][4][8752] where
[fn_idx][0] belonged, and the recursion dispatched through the
clobber. The fuel: assoc_row/esc_assoc scanned a 2,500-entry assoc
list via drop_last, minting a 16-byte slice per step — ~40KB per
lookup, ~20 lookups per fn, 2,500 fns per round: ~2GB PER ROUND of
escaping_round, on top of infer's ~2GB.

The Carried-Truth cut: callee names resolve to base POSITIONS once at
collect (base_index_find/resolve_callee_indices — a miss is dropped
there, once, not re-missed every round); rounds are rows-only lists
read by list_index — zero allocation, zero name scans; the name-keyed
view ls_escaping_of consumes is zipped once at the end. assoc_row is
deleted; esc_assoc walks by index (no slices).

The ratchet: the emitted $alloc now TRAPS on wrap — br_if 0 returns
the pointer on the sane path, fallthrough is unreachable — so any
future ceiling is a loud trap AT the allocator, never a silent
sub-4096 mint corrupting dispatch three functions later. Both layers
emit the same body (seed template relocated 1275→8080 for the larger
text; the wheel's runtime-contract string matches byte-for-byte).

Board: verify 37/37 through the seed, micros-through-m2 37/37 (the
battery ran ON the wrap-trapping allocator).
